history.summary: A 99-LH Pasir Ris 3BR with a genuine dated catalyst — the future Elias MRT (Cross Island Line, ~2030) is within walking distance. But asking $1,213 psf is at the TOP of the project's 12-month range, so the algo's 'cheap' signals are misleading.
history.rating_rationale: Two findings pull in opposite directions. Positive: a real, dated catalyst — LTA's Cross Island Line Elias station (CRL Phase 1, est. completion ~2030, walking distance), the kind of physical evidence v3.4 says can support a stronger call. D18 is OCR (favorable realized fwd ~+4.0%), and the development is large (388 units), well-landscaped and family-friendly. Negative, and decisive for confidence: the dossier's -16.1% age-adj 'cheap' and 'very_low_psf' flag do NOT survive a building-level check. Recent 12-month transactions average ~$1,158 psf (range $1,100-$1,222), so the asking $1,213 psf is at the upper end of the range — this unit is priced rich for the building, not cheap. The strongest robust forward signal (verified cheapness vs recent comps) is therefore absent; the case rests almost entirely on the CRL catalyst, which is 4+ years out and partly already in the price. With ~80 yrs lease left and an entry at the top of the band, the catalyst and the rich pricing roughly cancel. Trailing 8.87% CAGR (82 txns) is credible data but ~0 forward power, so I do not lean on it. Net: a defensible hold for the MRT story, but not a value buy — Neutral, leaning mildly positive.

history.summary: A standard 1,410 sqft 4BR at Oasis @ Elias (99-LH from 2008, completed 2011, 388 units, 70 Elias Road) asking $1,938,000 / $1,374 psf. The 717 score is almost entirely the project's 8.87%/yr trailing URA CAGR — re-scored at the OCR forward baseline (3.7%) the same unit prints 604, and its other positive term, '-6.8% cheap vs age-adjusted D18 peers', is a sub-market level Oasis has carried every single year (-5.5% in 2021, -7.1% 2022, -7.5% 2023, -8.3% 2026) and has never closed. Against the project's own prints there is no cushion at all: the last 1,410 sqft print was $1,197 psf (Oct-2024, floor 11-15) and the 1,400-1,500 sqft band has moved only ~+3% since ($1,310 psf Aug-2024 -> $1,353 psf Feb-2026, floor 16-20), so this ask is +14.8% over its own last same-size print and at or above a floor-adjusted read of the band's all-time high. Decisively for THIS listing: the identical unit (unit_group 'oasis elias|4|366', same 1,410 sqft) is live with another agent at $1,918,000 and has not cleared since 8-Jun-2026.
history.rating_rationale: Overpriced against its own comp set, and strictly dominated by a cheaper live ask on the same unit. (1) No value cushion: the algo's own psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct is +4.9% (a PREMIUM, on 5 cohort txns); vs the last 1,410 sqft print ($1,688,000 / $1,197 psf, Oct-2024, floor 11-15) the ask is +14.8% while the project's 1,400-1,500 sqft band rose only ~3% over the same window. A floor-adjusted read off the single Feb-2026 print (1,496 sqft, $1,353 psf, floor 16-20; ~3%/tier) puts a mid-floor 1,410 sqft unit near $1,310 psf / ~$1,847,000 — the ask carries ~5% of air unless this is a top-floor stack, which is unverified. (2) The score is a de-weighted signal: score_1000 717 rests on appreciation +14.61 of a +32.8 total MMR margin; at the OCR forward baseline of 3.7%/yr it is 604, below the 650 gate. The trailing 8.87% is genuine (size mix is stable: median print sqft 1206-1216 every year 2021-2025, so it is NOT the pooled-CAGR mix artifact) but trailing CAGR has ~0 measured forward power. (3) The remaining positive, age_value +5.37 from '-6.8% vs age-adjusted D18', is a permanent location level for the Elias Road pocket, not a dislocation — the gap has been -5.5%/-7.1%/-7.5%/-8.3% in 2021/22/23/26 and never closed. (4) Same unit asked $20k cheaper: listing 500059669 (Joey Tan), 1,410 sqft, $1,918,000, live since 8-Jun-2026 and unsold; this listing is the same unit re-marketed by a second agent at a higher number. (5) Thin exit in this size band: ZERO prints in the 1,350-1,550 sqft band in all of 2025 and ~18 in five years, against ~76 4BR units — the 1,200-1,300 sqft 3BR band is where the project's liquidity actually is. (6) Carry is weak: ~$5,000/mo (URA rental filings show 4BR 1,400-1,500 sqft at $4,900 May-26 and $5,100 Jun-26) = 3.1% gross, ~1.7% net, 1.1-1.3km / 15-16 min from Pasir Ris MRT. The unit itself is fine — a normal 4BR (3 baths), not the 9 duplex penthouses, and bed_bands returns 'ok' against the project's own URA 4BR rental band. It is the price that fails.

The identical unit is live $20k cheaper: listing 500059669, same unit_group 'oasis elias|4|366', same 1,410 sqft, $1,918,000, on market since 8-Jun-2026 and still unsold — this listing is that unit re-marketed by a second agent (Eileen Koh vs Joey Tan) at a higher ask

Thin exit liquidity for THIS size: zero URA prints in the 1,350-1,550 sqft band in all of 2025, ~18 in five years against ~76 4BR units; the project's real liquidity sits in the 1,200-1,300 sqft 3BR band

Floor is unverified (PropertyGuru serves no floor_level for this listing) and it is the swing factor — the sole 2026 large-unit print at $1,353 psf was floor 16-20, and same-size prints range $972-$1,197 psf across floor bands
Weak carry: ~3.1% gross / ~1.7% net yield at $5,000/mo; realsmart puts the project's estimated yield at 3.2%
Poor transit: 1.12-1.32 km / 15-16 min walk to Pasir Ris MRT; PropertyLimBrothers' MOAT scores the project weakest on exactly MRT Effect, Region Disparity and Rental Demand

The rest of the project's live book is asking even further above prints ($1,521-$1,536 psf on the 1,249 sqft 3BR and the 1,432 sqft 4BR) — asks at Oasis have run ahead of transactions, so 'cheapest in the book' is not the same as cheap
realsmart: 19 of 261 matched resale pairs (6.9%) exited unprofitable — a real, deeply-sampled loss rate; REALSCORE 3.4 is middling, below neighbouring Belysa (4.2)
99-yr lease from 17/03/2008 — 81-82 yrs left now, ~75 at a 5-7yr exit; a mild persistent drag with no freehold optionality
catalysts: Cross Island Line makes Pasir Ris an EWL x CRL interchange in 2030, ~900m straight-line away — the one dated, real catalyst, but the future-infrastructure score has no measured forward power in this repo's backtest, so treat it as narrative

A second CRL station named Elias opens 2032 on the Punggol Extension — but it is sited at the Pasir Ris Drive 3 / Drive 10 junction, not on Elias Road, and 2032 sits at or past the end of a 5-7yr hold bought in 2026; do not price it as a doorstep station
OCR / D18 — the region with the strongest realized forward drift in the backtest (OCR +3.7%/yr vs CCR +1.9%)
Genuine school catchment: Park View Primary 251m, Elias Park Primary 398m, Meridian Primary 746m — supports the owner-occupier floor (62% of the project's buyers are HDB upgraders)
Elias Mall, coffee shops, supermarket and clinics immediately adjacent — a durable convenience floor for a car-owning family buyer

Deep project-level exit record: 635 lifetime transactions, 93.1% of 261 matched resale pairs profitable, avg holding 6.7 yrs — the development is not a value trap, even though this size band is illiquid

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Weak-to-adequate. URA rental filings for the project put 4BR units of 1,400-1,500 sqft at $4,900 (May-26) and $5,100 (Jun-26); the DB's $4,750 (ura_project_bed, 6 contracts) is slightly conservative. At $5,000/mo the ask yields 3.1% gross and ~1.7% net — realsmart's project-level estimate is 3.2%. Tenant demand here is the weakest axis of the development: 1.1-1.3km from Pasir Ris MRT with no LRT and no employment node, so the pool is family tenants who need a car, not the expat/CBD-commuter pool that pays up. 21 contracts across the whole 388-unit project in the past month is respectable volume, but the $3,875 median rent shows it is a 2-3BR letting market; a 4BR at $5,000 is the thin top of it. Yield is carry only and, per the repo's priors, carries no appreciation signal either way.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The trailing number is real but not forward-usable. Decomposing the project's own URA prints by size shows the 8.87%/yr CAGR is NOT the pooled-mix artifact — median print size is 1206-1216 sqft every year from 2021 to 2025 — and both bands really did move (1,350-1,550 sqft: $982 psf 2021 -> $1,353 psf 2026, ~6.6%/yr; 940-1,050 sqft: $852 -> $1,154, ~7.9%/yr). But that is trailing CAGR off a 2021 trough, and the backtest gives it ~0 marginal forward power. What matters more is that the large-unit band has effectively stalled: $1,310 psf in Aug-2024 to $1,353 psf in Feb-2026 is ~+2.2%/yr, and 2025 produced no print in the band at all. realsmart's own past-1y annualized profit is 3.6%. The defensible forward number is the OCR baseline of ~3.7%/yr, not 8.87% — and buying at $1,374 psf, above a floor-adjusted read of the band's high print, hands back roughly the first year and a half of that before transaction costs. No appreciation_rate_override_pct is set: the honest forward rate is the region baseline the scorer already knows, and overriding at 3.7 would just be re-labelling the region term.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Oasis @ Elias (stack_profile: not_researched) and PropertyGuru serves no floor_level or facing for this listing, so the single largest price variable is unverified. What is known from the development: six blocks, most units face northeast or southwest, Block 72 is angled north-south, and high floors in Blocks 66/68/70 overlook the Straits of Johor to the northeast — the address here is 70 Elias Road, so a high floor in this block would be the good half of the project. The unit is a standard 4BR (1,410 sqft, 3 baths), which the developer's layout is a 3BR plan plus an ensuite junior master; it is NOT one of the 9 duplex penthouses (~2,637 sqft, one of which printed $902 psf in Apr-2023), so there is no strata/loft format artifact behind the numbers. bed_bands returns 'ok' — the project's URA rental 4BR band starts at 1,450 sqft with a 1,400-1,500 sqft bucket in the filings, so 1,410 sqft as a 4BR is consistent and this is not a relabel. Floor matters concretely: same-size 1,410 sqft prints run $972 (fl 11-15, 2021) to $1,197 psf (fl 11-15, 2024), and the only 2026 large print, $1,353 psf, was floor 16-20. If this unit is floor 16-20 and northeast-facing the ask is roughly fair; anything below that and it is rich. Verify before any counter-offer — and run /research-development on Oasis @ Elias first, since the project has three other live listings.
